correctness.rationale: For n>=2, side exchange τ sends a_i b_j to a_j b_i; geometric fixed-point coordinates are constant on edge orbits. Singletons d_i=a_i b_i map to cone edges 0i; offdiagonal pairs q_ij to edges ij. Selection lifts to forest in K_nn iff offdiagonal base F is forest and at most one diagonal is chosen per F-component; the same criterion defines a forest in K_(n+1). This is a PL S_n-equivariant simplicial identification. Coloopless graphic matroid shellability gives fixed wedge of b_n=T_{K_(n+1)}(0,1) spheres dim n−1 and ambient wedge of a_n=T_{K_nn}(0,1) spheres dim 2n−2; Lefschetz yields trace (-1)^(n−1)b_n, and rational 2-eigen splitting/transfer yields remaining formulas. Independent exhaustive orbit checks n2..5 found fixed Betti 1,6,51,560; direct signed ambient chains n2..4 found (rank,trace)=(1,-1),(20,6),(1071,-51). This is correct as mathematics, but its fixed-space theorem is a specialization of published general cone theorem.

originality.rationale: The published full Resultary source “A cone-graph model for the layer-swap fixed forest complex of a bipartite double cover” proves the same canonical Aut(G)-equivariant PL homeomorphism for EVERY finite simple graph G. Setting G=K_n gives the same B(G)=K_{n,n} and cone K_{n+1}, with the same spheres 1,6,51,560 explicitly stated. Candidate S_n PL fixed-locus theorem and fixed-space Betti counts are therefore immediate special cases. The remaining rational top trace/eigenspace/quotient formulas follow mechanically from the classical Lefschetz fixed point identity, coloopless graphic-matroid shellability, and rational transfer. The final claim is covered despite different title and appended corollaries.
